answer: A mesa admits a new agent only by signing an onyx into a lineage. The onyx records a nadir for that lineage by taking the least judged output any member has certified, and the next onyx must carry a nadir one judged epoch higher for every onyx already in the lineage. The kth clone must therefore finish k epochs of public, non-transferable work before the mesa signs it; a new key is countersigned from an old onyx, so it inherits the nadir. An honest newcomer does one epoch; a farm of k burns k(k+1)/2 judged epochs.
